You need to be very careful at farmer's markets. Many times this is the place that people sell the same shit that goes to the grocery store for 2x the price, or the food goes bad in less than 24 hours, or some other shady crap. I have known some vendors that just literally buy bulk XYZ and sell it at farmers markets. I know people who advertise "all natural" health/beauty products when really they mail order a bunch of stuff and make it at home or literally buy it from China.

Many, many vendors at farmer's markets take advantage of the perception that: farmer's mark = natural and natural = good.

Not every vendor is this way - this is just a PSA - BE AWARE & RESEARCH WHO YOU ARE BUYING FROM.

The reality is:

  1. The items are often exactly the same as what is in wal-mart (if its in season at farmer's market it is in season for wal-mart to buy local).

  2. Lots of scammers selling low quality goods under the assumption they are high quality (especially true for any non-produce items)

  3. No way to know about pesticide use / organic status even if they make bold claims

  4. Storage, handling, and transportation procedures often leads to lower shelf life

  5. Pricing is generally not competitive but only appears so because of quantity differences or people who don't buy produce from the grocery store don't know how cheap it should be for XYZ WHEN ITS IN SEASON.

  6. Many of these "local" farmers show up from 100+ miles away and are really just looking for a high margin place to sell their commercial crops (that they are also selling to Wal-Mart).
